sources_considered.why: Primary workplace research documents actual deskilling and qualifications. Its 2021–2022 interviews predate the target period and generative-AI rollout.
Read the paper. Its workforce analysis covers 2010–2018 and does not test the claimed 2023 managerial mechanism or inadequate-output condition.
Read the survey disclosure. Workforce reduction, redeployment and hiring do not measure reclassification as unskilled.

receipt.public_excerpt: not all skill decreases imply deskilling overall.

evidence_items.explanation: The study's interview collection ended in 2022 and included employers describing reduced skill requirements after automation, alongside qualifications about overall deskilling. It does not establish an increasing 2023 practice driven by merely theoretical AI capability despite inadequate output.

unresolved_gaps: No longitudinal record establishes increasing reclassification during the target period.
No matched corporate record links perceived AI substitutability, inadequate output and treatment of work as unskilled.
Earlier evidence of actual task automation does not establish the claimed generative-AI mechanism.
Available staffing surveys do not measure managerial valuation of skill.
